title: Who are the top consulting firms, and how are they usually grouped?
description: A map of the consulting world: MBB, the Big Four and their strategy arms, Accenture, other strategy firms, specialists and boutiques.
hook: Consulting has its own shorthand, MBB, Big Four, tier two, boutiques, and it can feel like everyone else already knows the map. Here it is in one place, so you can decide where to apply with a clear picture of what each group does.
body:
MBB: McKinsey, BCG and Bain

The three best-known strategy firms, often called the Big Three. They focus mainly on strategy and senior-level problems, though all three also do operations and implementation work. Their interviews are among the most competitive. How McKinsey, BCG and Bain differ.

The Big Four: Deloitte, PwC, EY and KPMG

Huge professional services firms that started in audit and accounting and now also offer tax, advisory and consulting. Together they earned around $220 billion in fiscal 2025 and employ well over a million people. Their consulting is broad, with large technology and implementation practices, plus dedicated strategy arms:

  • Deloitte: Monitor Deloitte (Deloitte acquired Monitor Group in 2013)
  • PwC: Strategy& (formerly Booz & Company)
  • EY: EY-Parthenon
  • KPMG: its strategy group

More on the Big Four.

Accenture

A global professional services company best known for technology and operations, with a strategy consulting business too. Often compared with the Big Four. Accenture's interview process.

Other strategy firms

Oliver Wyman, Kearney, Roland Berger, L.E.K. Consulting, OC&C and Simon-Kucher are well-respected strategy firms, often strong in particular industries or regions. They are sometimes called tier two, but many people choose them for their culture or specialism. More on these firms.

Specialists and boutiques

Smaller firms that focus on one industry (healthcare, energy), one function (pricing, people) or one region. They can offer earlier responsibility and deep expertise.

In-house strategy teams

Many large companies have their own internal strategy or transformation teams, often staffed by former consultants. They hire through similar case-style interviews.

How to use this map

Do not apply only to the names you know. Think about the work you want (strategy, operations, technology), the industries that interest you and the city you want to live in, then build a list across several groups.
